questions.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & -1 \\ -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ are eigenvectors that correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=-3$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=2$ of the matrix $A,$ given above. Find the third eigenvector ${v}_{3}=[a,\,b,\,c]^{T}$ such that the set $\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}\}$ is linearly independent. What is the value of $\frac{a}{b}?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find all the eigenvalues of $A$ by solving the characteristic equation $det(A-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-2-\lambda  & 0 & -2 \\ 1 & -1-\lambda  & -1 \\ -2 & 0 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-1-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}-2-\lambda  & -2 \\ -2 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-1-\lambda )((-2-\lambda )(1-\lambda )-(-2)(-2)) & =0 \\ (-1-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}+\lambda -6) & =0 \\ (\lambda +1)(\lambda +3)(\lambda -2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, ${\lambda }_{1}=-3,$ ${\lambda }_{2}=2,$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=-1.$ Since we obtained three distinct eigenvalues, the set of eigenvectors $\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}\},$ where each vector corresponds to different eigenvalue, will be linearly independent.

Now, recall that ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=-3$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=2.$ Thus, the third eigenvector ${v}_{3}$ must correspond to ${\lambda }_{3}=-1.$ 

To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =-1.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & -1 \\ -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]-(-1)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & -2 \\ 1 & 0 & -1 \\ -2 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}-2{x}_{3}=0 \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{3}=0 \\ -2{x}_{1}+2{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & -1 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 6 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+2{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $3$rd). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{3}=0.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}=0.$
Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 \\ {x}_{2} \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the following eigenvector:

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, $\frac{a}{b}=\frac{0}{1}=0.$

questions.problem:
Find an eigenvector of $A=[\begin{aligned}-9 & 9 & -7 \\ -14 & 13 & -8 \\ -2 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]$
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =3.$
questions.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =3.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}-9 & 9 & -7 \\ -14 & 13 & -8 \\ -2 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]-3[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-12 & 9 & -7 \\ -14 & 10 & -8 \\ -2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-12{x}_{1}+9{x}_{2}-7{x}_{3}=0 \\ -14{x}_{1}+10{x}_{2}-8{x}_{3}=0 \\ -2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-12 & 9 & -7 & 0 \\ -14 & 10 & -8 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}↔{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & -1 & 0 \\ -14 & 10 & -8 & 0 \\ -12 & 9 & -7 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-7){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-6){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{2}=\frac{1}{3}{x}_{3}.$ Substituting this in the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =-\frac{1}{2}(-{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}(-(\frac{1}{3}{x}_{3})+{x}_{3}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}{x}_{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{3}{x}_{3} \\ \frac{1}{3}{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{3}=3,$ we get the eigenvector
$v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$

questions.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 4 \\ 2 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ are eigenvectors that correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=-1$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=3$ of the matrix $A,$ given above. Find the third eigenvector ${v}_{3}=[a,\,b,\,c]^{T}$ such that the set $\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}\}$ is linearly independent. What is the value of $\frac{a}{c}?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find all the eigenvalues of $A$ by solving the characteristic equation $det(A-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 2 & 4 \\ 2 & 1-\lambda  & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & -2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-2-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 2 \\ 2 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-2-\lambda )((1-\lambda )(1-\lambda )-(2)(2)) & =0 \\ (-2-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-2\lambda -3) & =0 \\ (\lambda +2)(\lambda +1)(\lambda -3) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, ${\lambda }_{1}=-1,$ ${\lambda }_{2}=3,$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=-2.$ Since we obtained three distinct eigenvalues, the set of eigenvectors $\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}\},$ where each vector corresponds to different eigenvalue, will be linearly independent.

Now, recall that ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=-1$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=3.$ Thus, the third eigenvector ${v}_{3}$ must correspond to ${\lambda }_{3}=-2.$ 

To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =-2.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 4 \\ 2 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}]-(-2)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 4 \\ 2 & 3 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+4{x}_{3}=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}-4{x}_{3}=0 \\ 0=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 4 & 0 \\ 2 & 3 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-\frac{2}{3}){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{5}{3} & -\frac{20}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{2}=4{x}_{3}.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =\frac{1}{3}(-2{x}_{2}-4{x}_{3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(-2(4{x}_{3})-4{x}_{3}) \\  & =-4{x}_{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-4{x}_{3} \\ 4{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{3}=1,$ we get the following eigenvector:

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, $\frac{a}{c}=\frac{-4}{1}=-4.$

questions.problem:
Find an eigenvector of $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 5 & -4 \\ 0 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}]$
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =3.$
questions.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =3.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 5 & -4 \\ 0 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}]-3[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 \\ 0 & 2 & -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=0 \\ 2{x}_{2}-4{x}_{3}=0 \\ 2{x}_{2}-4{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{2}=2{x}_{3}.$ Substituting this in the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}(2{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(4{x}_{3}-2{x}_{3}) \\  & ={x}_{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{3} \\ 2{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{3}=1,$ we get the eigenvector
$v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

questions.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 0 & -4 \\ 3 & -3 & -3 \\ -4 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ are eigenvectors that correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=4$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-3$ of the matrix $A,$ given above. Find the third eigenvector ${v}_{3}=[a,\,b,\,c]^{T}$ such that the set $\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}\}$ is linearly independent. What is the value of $\frac{a}{b}?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find all the eigenvalues of $A$ by solving the characteristic equation $det(A-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-4-\lambda  & 0 & -4 \\ 3 & -3-\lambda  & -3 \\ -4 & 0 & 2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-3-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}-4-\lambda  & -4 \\ -4 & 2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-3-\lambda )((-4-\lambda )(2-\lambda )-(-4)(-4)) & =0 \\ (-3-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}+2\lambda -24) & =0 \\ (\lambda +3)(\lambda +6)(\lambda -4) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, ${\lambda }_{1}=4,$ ${\lambda }_{2}=-3,$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=-6.$ Since we obtained three distinct eigenvalues, the set of eigenvectors $\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2},{v}_{3}\},$ where each vector corresponds to different eigenvalue, will be linearly independent.

Now, recall that ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ correspond to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=4$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-3.$ Thus, the third eigenvector ${v}_{3}$ must correspond to ${\lambda }_{3}=-6.$ 

To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =-6.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 0 & -4 \\ 3 & -3 & -3 \\ -4 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]-(-6)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -4 \\ 3 & 3 & -3 \\ -4 & 0 & 8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-4{x}_{3}=0 \\ 3{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3}=0 \\ -4{x}_{1}+8{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -4 & 0 \\ 3 & 3 & -3 & 0 \\ -4 & 0 & 8 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 3 & 0 \\ -4 & 0 & 8 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+4{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{2}=-{x}_{3}.$ From the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}=2{x}_{3}.$
Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}2{x}_{3} \\ -{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{3}=1,$ we get the following eigenvector:

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, $\frac{a}{b}=\frac{2}{-1}=-2.$
